--remove-source-files should remove the source files as they are transferred and without any delays.
Canceling the operation should not result in duplicates remaining

With --remove-source-files, delete each source file immediately after its transfer finishes.
If I abort the operation, no extra copy of a file already sent should remain.

Canceling the operation may result in duplicates remaining.

With --remove-source-files, remove only the first source file to finish transferring, immediately after it transfers.
Canceling the operation should leave no duplicate of that first file.

`--remove-source-files` should not delete sources that are the same as targets
because targets would be deleted too!

With `--remove-source-files`, skip removal whenever a source and destination share the very same path.
Removing that source would also remove the destination.

because targets would be deleted too!
`--remove-source-files` should not delete sources that are the same as targets

`--remove-source-files` may delete sources that are the same as targets
even if their targets are deleted too.

With `--remove-source-files`, skip removal only for the first source in the transfer list whose path is also its target path.
Removing that source would also remove its target.

`--remove-source-files` should not delete those sources
because targets would be deleted too!
